answer: A practical defence is signed import export licence with customs attestation. It rests on a licence customs granted after a compliance audit, which gives every honest agent a echo that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since a licence customs granted after a compliance audit takes calendar time as well as money — and the reef is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The nebula is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
